<meta name="description" content="The Human Development (HD) Bachelor of Science is designed to support student learning about the mechanisms of growth and change across the lifespan. With areas of focus in developmental science, educational psychology and statistical methodology, HD majors will explore the biological, social, emotional, and cognitive processes of learning and development from conception to old age in diverse social and cultural contexts. Join us in exploring the complexities of human development and making a positive impact in the lives of others." />

  <div class="program_overview">
    
  <div class="clearfix text-formatted wysiwyg field field--name-body field--type-text-with-summary field--label-above">
    <div class="field__label">Program Overview </div>
              <div class="field__item">          <p>The Human Development program focuses on the study of how an individual changes across the lifespan and more specifically, examines how peers, families, schools, and cultures influence an individual's thinking and behavior. You will learn how people learn, think, and how our social interactions shape us. From conception to old age, you'll explore how these processes happen in diverse social and cultural contexts.</p><h3>Key Features</h3><ul class="arrow"><li data-list-item-id="e66f1d098f11dedd9c88f50bda5304da9"><strong>Interdisciplinary Approach</strong>: Gain a broad understanding of human development across biological, psychological, sociological, and cultural domains.</li><li data-list-item-id="e19ecf04e6118e565d4bfa6b9f47f6109"><strong>Research Opportunities</strong>: Collaborate with renowned faculty and participate in cutting-edge research projects.</li><li data-list-item-id="e017b589aa13a0ac98075eb806b670964"><strong>Practical Experience</strong>: Engage in hands-on learning through internships and field experiences, applying theoretical knowledge in real-world settings. Our faculty have a successful record of placing our undergraduate research assistants into highly competitive internships at institutions such as NIH, Children’s National Medical Center, Kennedy Krieger, and top R1 universities.</li><li data-list-item-id="ecfc9daf1f83a00abae11e4e6156edac8"><strong>Honors Program</strong>. <meta charset="utf-8"><span style="background-color:transparent;color:#000000;font-family:Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:400;text-decoration:none;vertical-align:baseline;white-space:pre-wrap;">Students work closely with faculty to gain greater depth and knowledge about research and scholarship in human development.</span></li></ul>
          </div>
          </div>

  </div>

  <div class="program_content">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph-testimonial testimonial testimonial--full-width stat-group-bg-dark">

I knew that by joining this program, I would receive the same amount of care and love with every step I took.”
          </div>

<div id="jump-link-8837" class="js-jump-link-section">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-section-title field--type-string field--label-hidden field__item">          Learning Goals
          </div>
      
  </div>

  <div class="paragraph paragraph-heading heading">
  <div class="heading_rule heading_rule--red heading_rule--center">
    <div class="heading_rule__inner">
        <div class="h2">Learning Goals</div>

    </div>
  </div>
      <div class="heading_rule__text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-text field--type-text-long field--label-hidden wysiwyg field__item"><ul class="arrow"><li>Understand human development from cognitive, social-emotional, and physiological perspectives, considering environmental and cultural influences.</li><li>Develop critical thinking and scientific inquiry skills.</li><li>Recognize how diversity impacts development across the lifespan.</li><li>Enhance communication skills for scientific and theoretical discussions, with the ability to adjust for various audiences.</li><li>Prepare for the workforce through internships and externships in different sectors.</li></ul></div>
      
    </div>
  </div>

<div id="jump-link-8840" class="js-jump-link-section">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-section-title field--type-string field--label-hidden field__item">          Careers
          </div>
      
  </div>

  <div class="paragraph paragraph-heading heading">
  <div class="heading_rule heading_rule--red heading_rule--center">
    <div class="heading_rule__inner">
        <div class="h2">Career Options</div>

    </div>
  </div>
      <div class="heading_rule__text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-text field--type-text-long field--label-hidden wysiwyg field__item"><p>Human Development provides a strong foundation for advanced degrees or careers in a variety of areas:</p></div>
      
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="dividing_line dividing_line_rule--none dividing_line_spacing--small"></div>

        <div class="paragraph paragraph-box_list_s">
              
            <div class="field field--name-field-box-1-content field--type-text-long field--label-hidden wysiwyg field__item"><ul class="arrow"><li><strong>Education</strong>: Teaching, educational administration, curriculum development</li><li><strong>Healthcare</strong>: Health education, patient advocacy, hospital administration</li><li><strong>Social Services</strong>: Case management, counseling, social work</li><li><strong>Public Policy</strong>: Policy analysis, advocacy, program management</li><li><strong>Psychology</strong>: Clinical psychology, counseling, research</li></ul></div>
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-box-2-content field--type-text-long field--label-hidden wysiwyg field__item"><ul class="arrow"><li><strong>Law</strong>: Family law, mediation, legal advocacy</li><li><strong>Human Resources</strong>: Employee relations, training, organizational development</li><li><strong>Government Agencies</strong>: Program coordination, community outreach, public health</li><li><strong>Marketing &amp; Communications</strong>: Market research, public relations, community engagement</li><li><strong>Medicine &amp; Neuroscience: </strong>Doctor, research scientist</li></ul></div>
      
          </div>

        <div class="h2">Program Requirements</div>

    </div>
  </div>
      <div class="heading_rule__text">
      
            <div class="field field--name-field-text field--type-text-long field--label-hidden wysiwyg field__item"><p>This curriculum is thoughtfully crafted to offer you a holistic understanding of human development. With an emphasis on both theoretical knowledge and practical application, our program equips you with the skills and insights needed to make a positive impact in diverse settings and communities.</p><p><a class="button" href="https://education.umd.edu/sites/default/files/uploads/inline-files/Human%20Development%204%20Year%20Major%20Bench%20_%202601_0.pdf" data-entity-uuid="c3541d67-681e-4616-a746-186c5fdaf397" data-entity-type="file" data-entity-substitution="file" title="Human Development 4 Year Major Bench _ 2601_0.pdf">Program Requirements and 4-Year Plan</a></p></div>

<article about="/undergraduate/programs-pathways/agricultural-resource-economics" typeof="schema:WebPage" class="page node-id-2315 full clearfix">
      <div class="section__inner section--padded-top">
      <div class="expand">
        <div class="page-hero page-hero--with-text ">
            <div class="page-hero__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/agriculturalresourceeconomics.jpg?itok=rRzGwIkg') center/cover;"></div><div class="page-hero__inner">
                                  <div class="page-hero__wedge"></div>
                  <div class="page-hero__text">
                    <h2 class="page-hero__title">Agricultural &amp; Resource Economics</h2>
                  </div>
                            </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  
  
    
<div class="section__inner">
    
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--ip-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            <p><a href="https://arec.umd.edu/" target="_blank">Agricultural and Resource Economics (AREC)</a> is widely regarded as one of the top departments of its kind in the world, offering students outstanding education and training in applied economics and business. Our majors focus on the economics of the environment, natural resources, agriculture, and international development.</p>

<p>The AREC department offers degrees in Bachelor of Science (B.S.), Master of Science (M.S.), Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.).<br>
<br>
<a class="btn" href="https://arec.umd.edu/">Agricultural and Resource Economics Information</a><br>
AREC has three undergraduate programs of study:</p>

<ul>
	<li>Agribusiness</li>
	<li>Environmental &amp; Resource Economics</li>
	<li>Agricultural &amp; Resource Economics</li>
	<li>Global Poverty (Minor only)</li>
</ul>

<p>Learn more about each of the programs of study below.</p>

      </div>



  </div>
  
<div class="section__inner section--padded">
      <h2>Undergraduate Programs of Study</h2>
    
    <div class="flexible-spotlight">
  <div class="flexible-spotlight__content">
          <h3 class="flexible-spotlight__title">Agribusiness</h3>
              <p>Agribusiness includes courses taken in the College of Business and Management. In addition to two semesters in accounting, this field will expose you to upper-level courses in business finance, marketing, management and law.</p>
              <a href="https://www.arec.umd.edu/undergraduate/current-students/major-requirements" class="btn" target="_self">
      More Information
  </a>      </div>
  <!--<div class="flexible-spotlight__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/Agribusiness_0.jpg?itok=rrpyUjTM') center/cover;"></div>-->
<div class="flexible-spotlight__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/Agribusiness_0.jpg?itok=rrpyUjTM') center/cover;"></div></div>

  <div class="flexible-spotlight">
  <div class="flexible-spotlight__content">
          <h3 class="flexible-spotlight__title">Environmental &amp; Resource Economics</h3>
              <p>This concentration focuses on the application of economic concepts across a variety of issues related to natural resources, such as water quality, global warming, and the development of world economies.</p>
              <a href="https://www.arec.umd.edu/undergraduate/current-students/major-requirements" class="btn" target="_self">
      More Information
  </a>      </div>
  <!--<div class="flexible-spotlight__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/AREC%20Professor%20with%20Graph_0.jpg?itok=PoEd35nk') center/cover;"></div>-->
<div class="flexible-spotlight__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/AREC%20Professor%20with%20Graph_0.jpg?itok=PoEd35nk') center/cover;"></div></div>

  <div class="flexible-spotlight">
  <div class="flexible-spotlight__content">
          <h3 class="flexible-spotlight__title">Agricultural &amp; Resource Economics</h3>
              <p>This concentration provides students with the flexibility to select a field of study that fits their career interests.</p>
              <a href="https://www.arec.umd.edu/undergraduate/current-students/major-requirements/" class="btn" target="_self">
      More Information
  </a>      </div>
  <!--<div class="flexible-spotlight__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/AgriculturalEconomics_0.jpg?itok=ASQpGjlE') center/cover;"></div>-->
<div class="flexible-spotlight__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/AgriculturalEconomics_0.jpg?itok=ASQpGjlE') center/cover;"></div></div>



  </div>

    </div>
  
      <div class="section__inner section--padded">
        <p><a href="https://psla.umd.edu/undergraduate/degrees/agricultural-science-technology" target="_blank"><span>Agricultural Science and Technology</span></a><span> (AGST) is an interdisciplinary major for students who want to learn about sustainable agricultural practices, the cultivation of various crops and educating others through the context of cutting-edge agricultural technology.</span><br><br><a class="btn" href="https://psla.umd.edu/undergraduate/degrees/agricultural-science-technology" target="_blank"><span>Agricultural Science and Technology</span></a><br>The AGST department offers three programs of study, with&nbsp;degrees available in Bachelor of Science (B.S.)</p><ul><li><span>Agronomy</span></li><li><span>Environmental Horticulture</span></li><li><span>Agricultural &amp; Extension Education.&nbsp;&nbsp;</span></li></ul><p>Learn more about each of the programs of study below.</p>

    </div>
  
    
<div class="section__inner">
      <h2>Agronomy</h2>
    
    <div class="image-with-text">
      <figure role="group" class="align-left">
      <!--<img alt="Tractor in a field" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/p177274_482198907_5_0.jpg?itok=KyE_6s6E">-->
    <img alt="Tractor in a field" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/p177274_482198907_5_0.jpg?itok=KyE_6s6E">    </figure>
        <p><a href="https://psla.umd.edu/students/undergraduate/prospective-students-resources/agricultural-science-technology/" target="_blank">Agronomy students</a> will be educated in a broad range of agricultural disciplines which will provide them with a comprehensive education in crop, soil and animal sciences. Here at the University of Maryland, the focus of the program will be for students to gain a sustainable perspective of agronomy. Students will take a holistic that will integrate the science of agronomy through studies in areas such as Animal Science, Crop Science, Soil Science, Farm Management, and Pest Management.<br>
&nbsp;</p>
  </div>



  </div>
  
<div class="section__inner">
      <h2>Environmental Horticulture</h2>
    
    <div class="image-with-text">
      <figure role="group" class="align-left">
      <!--<img alt="Flowers" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/p177274_714642674_5.jpg?itok=YP7JH5cX">-->
    <img alt="Flowers" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/p177274_714642674_5.jpg?itok=YP7JH5cX">    </figure>
        <p><a href="https://psla.umd.edu/students/undergraduate/prospective-students-resources/agricultural-science-technology/" target="_blank">The Environmental Horticulture </a>specialization (Formerly Plant Sciences: Horticulture and Crop Production) is designed to lead students toward becoming an owner-operator or a manager in fields such as: environmental horticulture; greenhouse management; container nursery production; fresh fruit and vegetable production; and plant protection. For students who have a strong interest in education, numerous possibilities for rewarding careers also exist in agricultural extension, public gardens, and ornamental horticulture.</p>
  </div>



  </div>
  
<div class="section__inner">
      <h2>Agricultural &amp; Extension Education</h2>
    
    <div class="image-with-text">
      <figure role="group" class="align-left">
      <!--<img alt="Teacher standing in front of graph and diagram" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/p177274_360718182_5.jpg?itok=GjllPQSP">-->
    <img alt="Teacher standing in front of graph and diagram" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/p177274_360718182_5.jpg?itok=GjllPQSP">    </figure>
        <p><a href="https://psla.umd.edu/students/undergraduate/prospective-students-resources/agricultural-science-technology/agricultural/" target="_blank">Agricultural &amp; Extension Education</a>&nbsp;is a University of Maryland program that is a cooperative effort of the College of Agriculture and Natural resources and the College of Education. It is designed to prepare students to teach agriculture and related subjects in high school. Many high schools in Maryland and other states offer an agricultural curriculum that is associated with The National FFA Organization. There are two paths that students can take in preparation for a career as a high school agriculture teacher. Students can double major in Agricultural Science and Technology (AGST) and Secondary Education or students can earn a B.S. degree in AGST and a M.A. degree in education.</p>
  </div>



  </div>
  
<div class="section__inner section--padded">

<article about="/undergraduate/programs-pathways/animal-science" typeof="schema:WebPage" class="page node-id-2311 full clearfix">
      <div class="section__inner section--padded-top">
      <div class="expand">
        <div class="page-hero page-hero--with-text ">
            <div class="page-hero__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2022-06/ansc_umd_0.jpg?itok=SZbW_2_z') center/cover;"></div><div class="page-hero__inner">
                                  <div class="page-hero__wedge"></div>
                  <div class="page-hero__text">
                    <h2 class="page-hero__title">Animal Science</h2>
                  </div>
                            </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  
      <div class="section__inner section--padded">
        <p><a href="http://ansc.umd.edu/">Animal and Avian Sciences</a> provides a challenging program for academically talented students interested in the application of biology and technology to the care, management, and study of domestic and aquatic animals. For more information, visit the:<br><br><a class="btn" href="http://ansc.umd.edu/">Animal Science Website</a><br>The ANSC department has degrees available in Bachelor of Science (B.S.), Master of Science (M.S.), Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.).&nbsp; ANSC offers three undergraduate programs of study and five graduate programs of study.</p><table><thead><tr><th><em><strong>Undergraduate Programs:</strong></em></th><th><em><strong>Graduate Programs:</strong></em></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><ul><li>Animal Care &amp; Management</li><li>Science/ Pre-Professional</li></ul></td><td><ul><li>Animal Behavior &amp; Well-Being</li><li>Genetics &amp; Cell Biology</li><li>Reproduction &amp; Development</li><li>Nutrient Utilization &amp; Metabolism</li><li>Pathobiology and Infectious Diseases</li></ul></td></tr></tbody></table>

    </div>
  
    
<div class="section__inner section--padded-top">
      <h2>Undergraduate Programs of Study</h2>
    
    <div class="flexible-spotlight">
  <div class="flexible-spotlight__content">
          <h3 class="flexible-spotlight__title">Animal Care &amp; Management</h3>
              <p>Love animals? Interested in exploring careers that deal with the care and use of animals? The Department of Animal and Avian Sciences offers a specialized option in Animal Care and Management. This curriculum prepares you for a rewarding career in poultry and livestock production and related fields (animal nutrition, health, and allied industries.)</p>
              <a href="https://ansc.umd.edu/undergraduate/prospective-students/" class="btn" target="_self">
      More Information
  </a>      </div>
  <!--<div class="flexible-spotlight__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2026-08/animalcare.jpg?itok=KMkJR-e_') center/cover;"></div>-->
<div class="flexible-spotlight__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2026-08/animalcare.jpg?itok=KMkJR-e_') center/cover;"></div></div>

  <div class="flexible-spotlight">
  <div class="flexible-spotlight__content">
          <h3 class="flexible-spotlight__title">Science/ Pre-Professional</h3>
              <p>Prepares students for admission to veterinary, dental or medical schools and/or graduate school. Graduate school study can open the door to an exciting research career in specialty areas of animal or biological sciences such as genetics, nutrition, physiology or cell biology.</p>
              <a href="https://ansc.umd.edu/undergraduate/prospective-students/" class="btn" target="_self">
      More Information
  </a>      </div>
  <!--<div class="flexible-spotlight__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/science3.jpg?itok=u_hdRCpE') center/cover;"></div>-->
<div class="flexible-spotlight__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/science3.jpg?itok=u_hdRCpE') center/cover;"></div></div>



  </div>
  
<div class="section__inner section--padded">
      <h2>Graduate Programs of Study</h2>
    
    <div class="flexible-spotlight">
  <div class="flexible-spotlight__content">
          <h3 class="flexible-spotlight__title">Animal Behavior &amp; Well Being</h3>
              <p>Faculty in our animal behavior &amp; well-being group study the impacts of environmental stressors on the behavior and well-being of agricultural animals.</p>
              <a href="https://ansc.umd.edu/graduate/" class="btn" target="_self">
      More Information
  </a>      </div>
  <!--<div class="flexible-spotlight__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2025-08/CC_CA_177274_1779777288_4.jpg?itok=YEt6Sjcx') center/cover;"></div>-->
<div class="flexible-spotlight__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2025-08/CC_CA_177274_1779777288_4.jpg?itok=YEt6Sjcx') center/cover;"></div></div>

  <div class="flexible-spotlight">
  <div class="flexible-spotlight__content">
          <h3 class="flexible-spotlight__title">Genetics &amp; Cell Biology</h3>
              <p>The primary thrust of the Genetics and Cell Biology Group is to illuminate the molecular and cellular basis of complex biological systems using a multi-organismal and multi-faceted approach. The group comprises faculty that span across multiple disciplines with research focuses in basic and translational research and with implications for animal health and diseases and the environment.</p>
              <a href="https://ansc.umd.edu/graduate/" class="btn" target="_self">
      More Information
  </a>      </div>
  <!--<div class="flexible-spotlight__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/genetics3.jpg?itok=kUTrbHtB') center/cover;"></div>-->
<div class="flexible-spotlight__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/genetics3.jpg?itok=kUTrbHtB') center/cover;"></div></div>

  <div class="flexible-spotlight">
  <div class="flexible-spotlight__content">
          <h3 class="flexible-spotlight__title">Reproduction &amp; Development</h3>
              <p>The Reproduction and Development faculty possess a wide range of scientific expertise that, in many instances, spans multiple core research areas. Through both basic and applied research, our faculty continues to make important contributions to the fields of animal agriculture and the biomedical sciences.</p>
              <a href="https://ansc.umd.edu/graduate/" class="btn" target="_self">
      More Information
  </a>      </div>
  <!--<div class="flexible-spotlight__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/babysheep3.jpg?itok=WltrNRJU') center/cover;"></div>-->
<div class="flexible-spotlight__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/babysheep3.jpg?itok=WltrNRJU') center/cover;"></div></div>

  <div class="flexible-spotlight">
  <div class="flexible-spotlight__content">
          <h3 class="flexible-spotlight__title">Nutrient Utilization &amp; Metabolism</h3>
              <p>The Nutrient Utilization and Metabolism faculty possess expertise in both basic and applied research approaches to systemically address important nutritional issues facing animal agriculture at the local, state and national levels.</p>
              <a href="https://ansc.umd.edu/graduate/" class="btn" target="_self">
      More Information
  </a>      </div>
  <!--<div class="flexible-spotlight__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2025-08/297_257_177274_1611312273_5.jpg?itok=exWhqFcI') center/cover;"></div>-->
<div class="flexible-spotlight__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2025-08/297_257_177274_1611312273_5.jpg?itok=exWhqFcI') center/cover;"></div></div>

  <div class="flexible-spotlight">
  <div class="flexible-spotlight__content">
          <h3 class="flexible-spotlight__title">Pathobiology and Infectious Diseases</h3>
              <p>The major task for this pathogen-host interacting group is to decipher how hosts launch efficient immunity against infections, thus information obtained will be useful for the development of vaccine and control of infectious diseases. This group include faculty with expertise covering multiple disciplines in both basic and translational research.</p>
              <a href="https://ansc.umd.edu/graduate/" class="btn" target="_self">
      More Information
  </a>      </div>
  <!--<div class="flexible-spotlight__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/salmonella_ansc2.jpg?itok=CQuB7Kpu') center/cover;"></div>-->
<div class="flexible-spotlight__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/salmonella_ansc2.jpg?itok=CQuB7Kpu') center/cover;"></div></div>



  </div>

<article about="/undergraduate/programs-pathways/environmental-science-policy" typeof="schema:WebPage" class="page node-id-2321 full clearfix">
      <div class="section__inner section--padded-top">
      <div class="expand">
        <div class="page-hero page-hero--with-text ">
            <div class="page-hero__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2025-07/ensp_0.jpg?itok=e8Z7nvCd') center/cover;"></div><div class="page-hero__inner">
                                  <div class="page-hero__wedge"></div>
                  <div class="page-hero__text">
                    <h2 class="page-hero__title">Environmental Science &amp; Policy</h2>
                  </div>
                            </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  
      <div class="section__inner section--padded">
        <p><a href="https://ensp.umd.edu/home/" target="_blank"><strong>Environmental Science and Policy (ENSP)</strong></a> is a multidisciplinary program that produces problem solvers and leaders who are prepared to face today’s environmental challenges. ENSP is a unique undergraduate major co-sponsored by four colleges. Students acquire a foundational understanding in science and policy through core classes, and then advance to specialized training and experiences in one of many academic disciplines ranging from biology to geology, and anthropology to government and politics.<br>
<br>
<strong>Degrees Offered: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science and Policy</strong><br>
<br>
<a class="btn" href="https://ensp.umd.edu/about/">Environmental Science and Policy Information</a></p>

    </div>
  
    
<div class="section__inner">
      <h2>Programs of Study</h2>
    
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--ip-text paragraph--view-mode--default">
            <p>All ENSP students begin as<strong>&nbsp;<a href="https://ensp.umd.edu/node/137">"undeclared" in ENSP</a></strong>&nbsp;(AGNR),&nbsp;where they will complete approximately 2-3 semesters of lower-level "core" courses before declaring a specialization.&nbsp;</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>

      </div>



  </div>
  
<div class="section__inner">
      <h2>AGNR Specializations</h2>
    
  

  </div>
  
<div class="section__inner section--padded-top">
      <h2>Environment and Agriculture</h2>
    
    <div class="image-with-text">
      <figure role="group" class="align-left">
      <!--<img alt="Tractor in a yellow wheat field with a vibrant blue sky in the background." src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-09/Environment%26Agriculture.jpg?itok=vmvnW8N4">-->
    <img alt="Tractor in a yellow wheat field with a vibrant blue sky in the background." src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-09/Environment%26Agriculture.jpg?itok=vmvnW8N4">    </figure>
        <p>Both locally and internationally, there is increasing concern about how humans manage soils, use water, raise animals, and modify the genetic base of crops. This concentration prepares students to work in agroecology, agricultural land management and conservation, sustainable agriculture, integrated pest management, and production science.&nbsp;<br>
<br>
<a class="btn" href="https://ensp.umd.edu/concentrations/environment-and-agriculture/" target="_blank">Environment and Agriculture</a></p>
  </div>



  </div>
  
<div class="section__inner section--padded-top">
      <h2>Environmental Economics</h2>
    
    <div class="image-with-text">
      <figure role="group" class="align-left">
      <!--<img alt="Solar panels in a green, grassy field " src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-09/EnvEcon.jpg?itok=jr7J2-Mh">-->
    <img alt="Solar panels in a green, grassy field " src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-09/EnvEcon.jpg?itok=jr7J2-Mh">    </figure>
        <p>Economics&nbsp;is the study of the allocation of scarce resources. Economists study how incentives affect people's behavior. Environmental and natural resource economics is the application of the principles of economics to the study of how environmental and natural resources are developed and managed.&nbsp;<br>
<br>
<a class="btn" href="https://ensp.umd.edu/concentrations/environmental-economics/" target="_blank">Environmental Economics</a></p>
  </div>



  </div>
  
<div class="section__inner section--padded-top">
      <h2>Soil, Water, and Land Resources</h2>
    
    <div class="image-with-text">
      <figure role="group" class="align-left">
      <!--<img alt="Man digging in countryside as interested bystanders watch" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-09/Soilwaterlandresourcesnew.jpg?itok=ubTX2iOz">-->
    <img alt="Man digging in countryside as interested bystanders watch" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-09/Soilwaterlandresourcesnew.jpg?itok=ubTX2iOz">    </figure>
        <p>Soil forms an essential part of the environment, affecting or controlling most living things. Soil science draws from geology, geography and a variety of other natural and life sciences, focuses land use management at the watershed scale and provides an integrated knowledge of soil and water dynamics to control problems like non-point source pollution, wetland delineation, and land classification.&nbsp;<br>
<br>
<a class="btn" href="https://ensp.umd.edu/concentrations/soil-water-and-land-resources/" target="_blank">Soil, Water, and Land Resources</a></p>
  </div>



  </div>
  
<div class="section__inner section--padded-top">
      <h2>Wildlife Ecology and Management</h2>
    
    <div class="image-with-text">
      <figure role="group" class="align-left">
      <!--<img alt="ENSP student holding an animal for a kid to see at a community event" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2026-07/ensp_wildlife.jpg?itok=kKl9FwfQ">-->
    <img alt="ENSP student holding an animal for a kid to see at a community event" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2026-07/ensp_wildlife.jpg?itok=kKl9FwfQ">    </figure>
        <p>Today, the study of wildlife ecology is a rigorous science that spans biological scales&nbsp;from the genome to the biosphere. Methods include inventory techniques&nbsp;for population size and condition, physiological function, migratory patterns, habitat evaluation, and food web studies. Management of wildlife is especially challenging because it requires the very best ecological science as a foundation, in addition to a strong perspective in social science.<br><br><a class="btn" href="https://ensp.umd.edu/specializations/wildlife-ecology-and-management/" target="_blank">Wildlife Ecology and Management</a></p>
  </div>



  </div>
  
<div class="section__inner section--padded">

In addition to general education courses, students will take core required courses on fermentation science and participate in industrial internships for practical experiences and experiential learning with fermentation industries and possible placement in those companies." />

<article about="/undergraduate/programs-pathways/fermentation-science" typeof="schema:WebPage" class="page node-id-3753 full clearfix">
      <div class="section__inner section--padded-top">
      <div class="expand">
        <div class="page-hero page-hero--with-text ">
            <div class="page-hero__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2025-07/ferm_umd.jpg?itok=0BXKkAM_') center/cover;"></div><div class="page-hero__inner">
                                  <div class="page-hero__wedge"></div>
                  <div class="page-hero__text">
                    <h2 class="page-hero__title">Fermentation Science</h2>
                  </div>
                            </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  
      <div class="section__inner section--padded">
        <p>Fermentation Science will prepare students for workforce demand of the broadly defined fermentation industries that include beverages (beer, wine, distilled spirits and kombucha), vegetable foods (kimchi, tempeh and miso), dairy foods (cheese and yogurt) and biotechnology industries (biofuels and pharmaceuticals). In addition to general education courses, students will take core required courses on fermentation science and participate in industrial internships for practical experiences and experiential learning with fermentation industries and possible placement in those companies.<br>
<br>
In addition to providing competencies for several areas of work, the fermentation science major is designed specifically for certain professional industrial careers including the fermented food, alcoholic beverage and pharmaceutical products.<br>
<br>
The Fermentation Science major<strong>&nbsp;</strong>is concerned with the application of the fundamental principles of the physical, biological, and behavioral sciences and processing to understand the complex and heterogeneous materials recognized as the raw precursors or/and final food products and beverages of fermentation. The fermentation science major prepares students for careers not only in traditional food and alcoholic beverage industries but also the biotechnology fermentation industry for pharmaceutical and nutraceutical production.</p>

<p><a class="btn btn--small" href="https://nfsc.umd.edu/undergraduate/fermentation-science" target="_blank">Fermentation Science information</a></p>

    </div>

<article about="/undergraduate/programs-pathways/nutrition-food-science" typeof="schema:WebPage" class="page node-id-2338 full clearfix">
      <div class="section__inner section--padded-top">
      <div class="expand">
        <div class="page-hero page-hero--with-text ">
            <div class="page-hero__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/nutritionfoodscience.jpg?itok=tLzOPOFd') center/cover;"></div><div class="page-hero__inner">
                                  <div class="page-hero__wedge"></div>
                  <div class="page-hero__text">
                    <h2 class="page-hero__title">Nutrition &amp; Food Science</h2>
                  </div>
                            </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  
      <div class="section__inner section--padded">
        <p><a href="https://nfsc.umd.edu/">The Department of Nutrition and Food Science</a> (NFSC) in the College of Agriculture and Natural Resources offers two undergraduate majors for students who would like to pursue challenging careers in the growing field of food and nutrition. The program offers a Bachelor of Science degree in Fermentation Science and Nutrition and Food Science with three options for students interested in nutritional science, food science, and dietetics.</p>

<p>The Department of Nutrition and Food Science strives to prepare students for careers in the dynamic and global food industry, public health and community nutrition sectors, health care, or biomedical research. NFSC houses the University of Maryland College Park Dietetic Internship, as well as interdepartmental graduate programs in both Food Science and Nutrition.<br>
<br>
<a class="btn" href="https://nfsc.umd.edu/" target="_blank">Nutrition and Food Science information</a><br>
The NFSC department has degrees available in Bachelor of Science (B.S.), Master of Science (M.S.), Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.).&nbsp;</p>

    </div>
  
    
<div class="section__inner section--padded-bottom">
      <h2>Undergraduate Programs of Study</h2>
    
    <div class="image-with-text">
      <figure role="group" class="align-left">
      <!--<img alt="Man looking into a microscope with windows behind him" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/p177274_892023570_5_0.jpg?itok=uZf4q9mb">-->
    <img alt="Man looking into a microscope with windows behind him" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/p177274_892023570_5_0.jpg?itok=uZf4q9mb">    </figure>
        <h4>Nutritional science</h4>

<p>The Nutritional Science concentration (formerly known as Human Nutrition and Foods) focuses on the physiological and biological aspects of foods and nutrients. Opportunities for nutritional scientists include research positions in laboratories, hospitals, and industry. This option prepares students for graduate study. The program also meets premedical and pre-dental requirements.</p>

<p><a class="btn" href="https://nfsc.umd.edu/undergraduate/" target="_blank">More Information</a></p>
  </div>



  </div>
  
<div class="section__inner section--padded">
    
    <div class="image-with-text">
      <figure role="group" class="align-left">
      <!--<img alt="Woman conducting research" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/FoodScienceUndergrad.jpg?itok=Hy0INxUr">-->
    <img alt="Woman conducting research" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/FoodScienceUndergrad.jpg?itok=Hy0INxUr">    </figure>
        <h4>Food science</h4>

<p>The Food Science concentration prepares students to apply the principles of science and engineering to better understand the complex and heterogeneous materials recognized as food. There is a great demand in the global food industry and government for highly knowledgeable and competent food scientists. Opportunities for food scientists include food safety, food quality control, food product development, production management, technical sales and service, ingredient management, research, and teaching. This option also prepares students for graduate study.</p>

<p><a class="btn" href="https://nfsc.umd.edu/undergraduate/" target="_blank">More Information</a></p>
  </div>



  </div>
  
<div class="section__inner section--padded">
    
    <div class="image-with-text">
      <figure role="group" class="align-left">
      <!--<img alt="Professor and students in the classroom" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2026-09/dietetics.png?itok=qZeGH7wb">-->
    <img alt="Professor and students in the classroom" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2026-09/dietetics.png?itok=qZeGH7wb">    </figure>
        <h4>Dietetics</h4><p>The Dietetics concentration prepares students to apply their knowledge of nutrition to promote healthy eating patterns in the population. Registered Dietitians (RDs) work in many areas including clinical and community nutrition, nutrition counseling, nutrition education and research, wellness, government, public health, food service management and others. The dynamic field of Dietetics is ever growing and dietitians continue to find new and different ways to communicate nutrition information to the public. This option also prepares students for medical and dental school, as well as graduate study in a variety of fields.<br><br><a class="btn" href="https://nfsc.umd.edu/undergraduate/" target="_blank">More Information</a></p>
  </div>



  </div>
  
<div class="section__inner section--padded">
    
    <div class="image-with-text">
      <figure role="group" class="align-left">
      <!--<img alt="Student smiling while fermenting food with tubes going into two milk jugs" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/FermentationScience101.jpg?itok=BoAsXuan">-->
    <img alt="Student smiling while fermenting food with tubes going into two milk jugs" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/FermentationScience101.jpg?itok=BoAsXuan">    </figure>
        <h4>Fermentation science</h4>

<p>Fermentation Science will prepare students for workforce demand of the broadly defined fermentation industries that include beverages (beer, wine, distilled spirits and kombucha), vegetable foods (kimchi, tempeh and miso), dairy foods (cheese and yogurt) and biotechnology industries (biofuels and pharmaceuticals). In addition to general education courses, students will take core required courses on fermentation science and participate in industrial internships for practical experiences and experiential learning with fermentation industries and possible placement in those companies.&nbsp;<br>
<a class="btn" href="https://nfsc.umd.edu/undergraduate/" target="_blank">More Information</a></p>
  </div>



  </div>
  
<div class="section__inner section--padded">
      <h2>Additional Resources</h2>
    
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--ip-text paragraph--view-mode--default">

<article about="/undergraduate/programs-pathways/plant-science" typeof="schema:WebPage" class="page node-id-2344 full clearfix">
      <div class="section__inner section--padded-top">
      <div class="expand">
        <div class="page-hero page-hero--with-text ">
            <div class="page-hero__image" style="background: url('/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/plantscience.jpg?itok=2yy9q3c_') center/cover;"></div><div class="page-hero__inner">
                                  <div class="page-hero__wedge"></div>
                  <div class="page-hero__text">
                    <h2 class="page-hero__title">Plant Science</h2>
                  </div>
                            </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  
      <div class="section__inner section--padded">
        <p><a href="https://psla.umd.edu//" target="_blank"><span>The Plant Science</span></a><span> (PLSC) major in the Department of Plant Science and Landscape Architecture (PSLA) is composed of three concentrations: Plant Biology, Turf and Golf Course Management, and Urban Forestry. This major combines fundamental science coursework with applied technical classes to prepare students for a wide range of career options. We also offer a minor in Landscape Management.</span><br><br><a class="btn btn--small" href="https://psla.umd.edu//" target="_blank">Plant Science Information</a><br>Plant Sciences offers degrees in Bachelor of Science (B.S.), Master of Science (M.S.), Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.).<br><br>Plant Sciences has three undergraduate programs of study:</p><ul><li>Plant Biology</li><li>Turf &amp; Golf Course Management</li><li>Urban Forestry</li><li>Landscape Management (Minor only)</li></ul><p>Learn more about each of the programs of study below.</p>

    </div>
  
    
<div class="section__inner">
      <h2>Undergraduate Programs of Study</h2>
    
    <div class="image-with-text">
      <figure role="group" class="align-left">
      <!--<img alt="Woman standing in a field of plants" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/plantbio102.jpg?itok=OnNagt8C">-->
    <img alt="Woman standing in a field of plants" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/plantbio102.jpg?itok=OnNagt8C">    </figure>
        <h4>Plant biology</h4>

<p>The Plant Biology Program is intended as a preparatory curriculum that will qualify our graduates for postgraduate study in any aspect of Plant Biology. Whether the student is interested in working in the rapidly developing field of agricultural biotechnology or wishes to academically contribute to the creation of new knowledge in the plant sciences, this is the option that should be chosen.</p>

<p><a class="btn" href="https://psla.umd.edu/students/undergraduate/prospective-students-resources/plant-sciences/" target="_blank">More Information</a></p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>
  </div>



  </div>
  
<div class="section__inner">
    
    <div class="image-with-text">
      <figure role="group" class="align-left">
      <!--<img alt="Man leaning down inspecting turf" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/Turf.jpg?itok=32FJMVuL">-->
    <img alt="Man leaning down inspecting turf" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/Turf.jpg?itok=32FJMVuL">    </figure>
        <h4>Turf and golf course management</h4>

<p>The Turf and Golf Course Management Program at the University of Maryland provides students with the broad based skills needed to succeed as a practicing turfgrass professional. The program focuses on golf turf management but also has been designed to expose students to all segments of the turfgrass industry.</p>

<p><a class="btn" href="https://psla.umd.edu/students/undergraduate/prospective-students-resources/plant-sciences/" target="_blank">More Information</a></p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>
  </div>



  </div>
  
<div class="section__inner">
    
    <div class="image-with-text">
      <figure role="group" class="align-left">
      <!--<img alt="Student swinging from a tree" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/urbanforestry.jpg?itok=Ww6T_XBe">-->
    <img alt="Student swinging from a tree" src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/urbanforestry.jpg?itok=Ww6T_XBe">    </figure>
        <h4>Urban forestry</h4>

<p>Urban Forestry is managing our green infrastructure, by planting and maintaining trees in neighborhoods, open space, parks, and urban landscapes, protecting forests and trees during land development, beautifying roadsides, public properties, and cities. The Urban Forestry Program at the UMD offers the education and training to become an urban forester or continue studies in graduate programs in forestry and other related areas.<br>
<br>
<a class="btn" href="https://psla.umd.edu/students/undergraduate/prospective-students-resources/plant-sciences/" target="_blank">More Information</a></p>
  </div>



  </div>
  
<div class="section__inner">
    
    <div class="image-with-text">
      <figure role="group" class="align-left">
      <!--<img alt="Man raking with a red shirt on." src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/raking.jpg?itok=_j08tcgN">-->
    <img alt="Man raking with a red shirt on." src="/sites/agnr.umd.edu/files/styles/optimized/public/2024-08/raking.jpg?itok=_j08tcgN">    </figure>
        <h4>Landscape management (minor)</h4>

<p>The University of Maryland Landscape Management Program provides students with academic resources applicable to management positions within the horticulture and landscape industries. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in the plant sciences, which in combination with business management courses enables graduates to meet the challenges of industry, public horticulture, and entrepreneurship.<br>
<a class="btn" href="https://psla.umd.edu/students/undergraduate/current-students-resources/minors/" target="_blank">More Information</a></p>
  </div>



  </div>
  
<div class="section__inner section--padded">
    
    <div class="expand">
  <div class="video-wrapper">
    <iframe src="  https://www.youtube.com/embed/zjEQ3QGOENg?si=yqkjD0hD-VpFDwwf
" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen="" title=""></iframe>
  </div>
</div>
  <p><small></small></p>



  </div>

          <div class="widget gsc-heading align-left style-3 padding-bottom-20">
            <h2 class="node__title title"><span>
<span property="schema:name">General Information</span>
</span></h2>
          </div>
        </div>
      </header>
        <div class="node__content clearfix">
      
            <div property="schema:text" class="field field--name-body field--type-text-with-summary field--label-hidden field__item"><h3>Chemistry and Biochemistry are among the more structured majors on campus, meaning that a significant number of courses must be taken (and passed) in a particular sequence. It is important that majors and prospective majors carefully plan out each semester leading up to graduation. Majors must also meet <a href="https://chem.umd.edu/sites/default/files/CHEM-BCHM-Benchmarks-01-2024_0.pdf">certain benchmarks</a> as they progress through the major.</h3><p>The sample plans and check-sheets below are organized by program. <strong>Sample plans</strong> map out a suggested semester-by-semester sequence; <strong>check-sheets</strong> let you quickly evaluate your progress toward completing the major. These plans assume a student begins as a Chemistry or Biochemistry major in the first year, but they can be adapted to other situations, such as declaring later than the first year. <em>Not sure which set applies to you? Use the catalog year tied to the term you declared the major.</em></p><h3><br>Effective Fall 2026</h3><table class="table"><caption style="text-align:left;">Sample plans and check-sheets for the current catalog</caption><thead style="text-transform:uppercase;"><tr><th scope="col">Program</th><th scope="col">Sample 4-year plans</th><th scope="col">Check-sheets</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Chemistry (BS)</th><td><a href="https://chem.umd.edu/sites/default/files/chembiochbachelorprograms-f26.pdf">CHEM (BS/BA) &amp; BCHM (BS) comparison plans</a></td><td><a href="https://chem.umd.edu/sites/default/files/chemistrybs-checksheet-f26.pdf">Chemistry BS check-sheet</a></td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Biochemistry (BS)</th><td><a href="https://chem.umd.edu/sites/default/files/chembiochbachelorprograms-f26.pdf">CHEM (BS/BA) &amp; BCHM (BS) comparison plans</a></td><td><a href="https://chem.umd.edu/sites/default/files/biochemistrybs-checksheet-f26.pdf">Biochemistry BS check-sheet</a></td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Chemistry (BA)</th><td><a href="https://chem.umd.edu/sites/default/files/chembiochbachelorprograms-f26.pdf">CHEM (BS/BA) &amp; BCHM (BS) comparison plans</a></td><td><a href="https://chem.umd.edu/sites/default/files/chemistryba-checksheet-f26.pdf">Chemistry BA check-sheet</a></td></tr></tbody></table><h3><br>Effective Fall 2023 / Spring 2024</h3><table class="table"><caption style="text-align:left;">Sample plans and check-sheets for the Fall 2023 / Spring 2024 catalog</caption><thead style="text-transform:uppercase;"><tr><th scope="col">Program</th><th scope="col">Sample 4-year plans</th><th scope="col">Check-sheets</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Chemistry (BS)</th><td><a href="https://chem.umd.edu/sites/default/files/documents/CHEMBIOCHBachelorPrograms24.pdf">CHEM (BS/BA) &amp; BCHM (BS) comparison plans</a></td><td><a href="https://chem.umd.edu/sites/default/files/undergrad/ChemistryBS-Checksheet-F25.pdf">Chemistry BS check-sheet</a></td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Biochemistry (BS)</th><td><a href="https://chem.umd.edu/sites/default/files/documents/CHEMBIOCHBachelorPrograms24.pdf">CHEM (BS/BA) &amp; BCHM (BS) comparison plans</a></td><td><a href="https://chem.umd.edu/sites/default/files/documents/BiochemistryBS-Checksheet-S24.pdf">Biochemistry BS check-sheet</a></td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Chemistry (BA)</th><td><a href="https://chem.umd.edu/sites/default/files/documents/CHEMBIOCHBachelorPrograms24.pdf">CHEM (BS/BA) &amp; BCHM (BS) comparison plans</a></td><td><a href="https://chem.umd.edu/sites/default/files/documents/ChemistryBA-Checksheet-S24.pdf">Chemistry BA check-sheet</a></td></tr></tbody></table><h3><br>Archived — pre-Fall 2023 / pre-Spring 2024</h3><table class="table"><caption style="text-align:left;">Sample plans and check-sheets for earlier catalog years</caption><thead style="text-transform:uppercase;"><tr><th scope="col">Program</th><th scope="col">Sample 4-year plans</th><th scope="col">Check-sheets</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Chemistry</th><td><a href="https://chem.umd.edu/sites/default/files/CHEM-4-Year-Plan.docx">CHEM 4-year plan</a> (.docx)</td><td><a href="https://chem.umd.edu/sites/default/files/CHEM_cs_2016.pdf">Chemistry check-sheet</a></td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Biochemistry</th><td><a href="https://chem.umd.edu/sites/default/files/BCHM-4-Year-Plan%20(2).docx">BCHM 4-year plan</a> (.docx)</td><td><a href="https://chem.umd.edu/sites/default/files/BCHM_cs_2016.pdf">Biochemistry check-sheet</a></td></tr></tbody></table><h1><br>AP Chemistry Credit</h1><ul><li data-list-item-id="e559c76530803e30a47a8ae5c66b64a34">Students who got a 4 on the AP Chemistry exam (or an equivalent score on the IB exam, British A-Levels, etc.) will receive credit for CHEM 131 and CHEM 132. Students with chemistry AP scores of 4 can enter organic chemistry directly unless they are CHEM or a&nbsp; BCHM major, in which case they have to take CHEM 177 their first term.</li><li data-list-item-id="e233356cd023daac2a180d503abc9d917">Students who got a 5 on the AP chemistry exam (or an equivalent score on the IB exam, British A-Levels, etc), will receive credit for CHEM 131, CHEM 132, and CHEM 271. Students with chemistry AP scores of 5 can enter organic chemistry directly unless they are a CHEM or a&nbsp; BCHM major, in which case they have to take CHEM 177 their first term.&nbsp; PLEASE NOTE: Students with chemistry AP scores of 5 do not receive CHEM 272 credit and generally have to take the CHEM 272 laboratory to complete their chemistry requirements; consult with your program advisor.</li></ul><h1>American Chemical Society Certification</h1><p>Chemistry and Biochemistry majors can complete programs that are certified by the American Chemical Society (ACS). Chemistry and Biochemistry degrees certified by the ACS are guaranteed to have a specified level of content and rigor as defined by the ACS as essential for high level training in the discipline. Majors completing the certification requirements will receive a certificate from the ACS indicating their degree is ACS certified. To be certified:</p><ul><li data-list-item-id="e64d6821754f6037c092139fc48ca9471"><strong>Chemistry majors</strong>, as part of their program, must complete BCHM 461 or BCHM 463 as one of their upper level elective classes.</li><li data-list-item-id="e93f8ab185709f4afe8d5210b73f0e4ea"><strong>Biochemistry majors</strong>&nbsp;must complete CHEM 401 (Inorganic Chemistry) in addition to the rest of the major requirements. CHEM 401 is only offered in the spring semester.</li></ul></div>
      
    </div>
  </article>

                  <a id="main-content"></a>
                    <h1 class="page-header">Degree Requirements for CS Major</h1>
                                                          <div class="region region-content">
        <section id="block-system-main" aria-label="block-system-main" class="block block-system clearfix">
        <article id="node-36" class="node node-page clearfix" about="/degree-requirements-cs-major" typeof="foaf:Document">
    <header>
            <span property="dc:title" content="Degree Requirements for CS Major" class="rdf-meta element-hidden"></span>      </header>
    <div class="field field-name-body field-type-text-with-summary field-label-hidden"><div class="field-items"><div class="field-item even" property="content:encoded"><div class="panel-pane" id="jumpnav">
<ul class="nav nav-pills">
<li><a href="#required-lower-level-coursework">Required Lower Level Coursework</a></li>
<li><a href="#upper-level-concentration">Upper Level Concentration</a></li>
<li><a href="#lep-benchmarks">LEP Benchmarks</a></li>
<li><a href="#degree-requirements">Degree Requirements</a></li>
<li><a href="#academic-planning-forms">Academic Planning Forms</a></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="panel-pane">
<p class="lead">Much of the knowledge at the early stage of the degree program is cumulative. To ensure incoming first-year and transfer students start with the appropriate courses, the department offers exemption exams for CMSC131, CMSC132, CMSC216, and CMSC250. Students who have had CS courses prior to starting at Maryland are encouraged to take our <a href="http://undergrad.cs.umd.edu/node/24">exemption exams</a>.</p>
</div>
<div class="panel-pane" id="required-lower-level-coursework">
<h2>Required Lower Level Coursework</h2>
<p>All students, regardless of specialization, are required to take the following lower level coursework:</p>
<table class="table table-striped">
<tbody>
<tr class="active">
<th style="width:50%;">Math Requirements</th>
<th>Computer Science Requirements</th>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>
<ul>
<li>MATH140 (4) Calculus I</li>
<li>MATH141 (4) Calculus II</li>
<li>STAT4XX (3) This course must have a prerequisite of MATH141; <em>Cannot be crosslisted with CMSC</em></li>
<li>MATH/STATXXX (3/4) This course must have a prerequisite of MATH141; <em>Cannot be cross-listed with CMSC</em></li>
</ul>
<p>* Data Science, Machine Learning, and Quantum Information students must take a MATH Linear Algebra course (e.g. MATH240, MATH341 [must complete MATH340 first], or MATH461)</p></td>
<td>
<ul>
<li>CMSC131 (4) Object-Oriented Programming I<span style="color:">*</span> <strong>or</strong> CMSC133 (2) Object-Oriented Programming I Beyond Fundamentals</li>
<li>CMSC132 (4) Object-Oriented Programming II<span style="color:">*</span></li>
<li>CMSC216 (4) Introduction to Computer Systems<span style="color:">*</span></li>
<li>CMSC250 (4) Discrete Structures<span style="color:">*</span></li>
<li>CMSC330 (3) Organization of Programming Languages</li>
<li>CMSC351 (3) Algorithms</li>
</ul>
<p><span style="color:">*</span> An <a href="http://undergrad.cs.umd.edu/node/24">exemption exam</a> is available for this course.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<hr /></div>
<div class="panel-pane" id="upper-level-concentration">
<h2>Upper Level Concentration</h2>
<p>All students, regardless of specialization, must complete 12 credit hours of 300 - 400 level courses in one discipline <strong>outside</strong> of Computer Science with a cumulative GPA of 1.7 or higher in this coursework. No course that is in, or crosslisted as, CMSC may be counted in this requirement (e.g., AMSC460). Only 1 independent study or experiential learning course may be used. Students who are pursuing a minor or a double major/dual degree may use those credits in this area with the exception of a few majors/disciplines (e.g., Information Science). Please consult with your advisor to ensure the courses you plan to take to ensure they will satisfy this requirement. For a detailed breakdown of accepted Upper-Level Concentration courses please click <strong><a href="https://undergrad.cs.umd.edu/upper-level-concentration">here</a>.</strong></p>
<hr /></div>
<div class="panel-pane" id="lep-benchmarks">
<h2>Limited Enrollment Program (LEP) Benchmarks*</h2>
<p>* These benchmarks apply to new freshman (matriculated Fall 2019 and later), new transfer students, and internal transfers changing majors within the University *</p>
<p>All students will undergo a benchmark review at 45 and 75 credits. Students in the major are required to complete the following courses:</p>
<h3 style="font-weight: lighter"><em>45-Credit Benchmark Requirements</em></h3>
<ul style="margin: 0">
<li>Completion of CMSC 131 with a minimum grade of C-</li>
<li>Completion of CMSC 132 with a minimum grade of C-</li>
<li>Completion of MATH 140 with a minimum grade of C-</li>
<li>A minimum grade point average of 2.0 in all courses taken at the University of Maryland and all other institutions</li>
</ul>
<h3 style="font-weight: lighter"><em>75-Credit Benchmark Requirements</em></h3>
<ul style="margin: 0">
<li>Completion of CMSC 330 with a minimum grade of C-</li>
<li>Completion of CMSC 351 with a minimum grade of C-</li>
<li>Completion of a STAT4XX course (prerequisite: MATH141) with a minimum grade of C- <strong><u>or</u></strong> MATH/AMSC/STAT course (prerequisite: MATH141) with a minimum grade of C-</li>
<li>A minimum grade point average of 2.0 in all courses taken at the University of Maryland and all other institutions</li>
</ul>
<p> </p>
<p><strong>Please contact your advisor if you have concerns about meeting your benchmarks.</strong></p>
<hr /></div>
<div class="panel-pane" id="degree-requirements">
<h2>Degree Requirements</h2>
<p>Students within the Computer Science major may choose to pursue our General Track or one of four specializations offered. Students are not required to pursue a specialization but may find one best fits their interests. Students interested in declaring a specialization should speak with their assigned academic advisor.</p>
<p>Students, regardless of specialization, are required to fulfill their computer science upper level course requirements from at least 3 areas. Courses that fall within each area are listed in the General Track degree requirements. The five areas are: Area 1: Systems, Area 2: Information Processing, Area 3: Software Engineering and Programming Languages, Area 4: Theory, Area 5: Numerical Analysis.</p>
<p>For tracks allowing CMSC electives, three 1-credit CMSC STIC courses are equivalent to one 3-credit 300-400 level elective course. Visit <a href="https://stics.umd.edu/index.html">UMD's official STICs website</a> and our <a href="https://undergrad.cs.umd.edu/faq">FAQ page</a> for more information on STICs and see your assigned advisor for information on how STICs can fit into your specialization.</p>
<div class="row">
<div class="col-sm-6">
<div class="panel panel-default">
<div class="panel-heading">
<h3 class="card-title">Distributive Areas (All Tracks)</h3>
</div>
<div class="panel-body">
<p class="card-text">Regardless of track, all CS students must complete 5 Distributive Area courses from at least 3 different areas. This information outlines the General Track degree requirements and can be used by all 4 CS specialization tracks to identify courses that count toward distributive area requirements and CS upper-level elective requirements. Click on your track to learn more track-specific information.</p>
<p><a class="btn btn-primary" href="/general-track-degree-requirements" target="_blank" title="learn more about General Track">Learn More</a></p></div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="col-sm-6">
<div class="panel panel-default">
<div class="panel-heading">
<h3 class="card-title">Cybersecurity</h3>
</div>
<div class="panel-body">
<p class="card-text">The Cybersecurity Specialization allows students to have the necessary background to address myriad cybersecurity issues relevant to government, industry, and academic careers.</p>
<p><a class="btn btn-primary" href="/cybersecurity-degree-requirements" target="_blank" title="learn more about Cybersecurity">Learn More</a></p></div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="row">
<div class="col-sm-6">
<div class="panel panel-default">
<div class="panel-heading">
<h3 class="card-title">Data Science</h3>
</div>
<div class="panel-body">
<p class="card-text">Data Science is an emerging field encapsulating interdisciplinary activities, used to create data-centric products, applications or programs that address specific scientific, socio-political, or business questions.</p>
<p><a class="btn btn-primary" href="/data-science-degree-requirements" target="_blank" title="learn more about Data Science">Learn More</a></p></div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="col-sm-6">
<div class="panel panel-default">
<div class="panel-heading">
<h3 class="card-title">Quantum Information</h3>
</div>
<div class="panel-body">
<p class="card-text">The Quantum Information specialization allows students to capitalize on the recent advances toward the experimental realization of quantum computers together with significant ongoing work on the theory of quantum computing.</p>
<p><a class="btn btn-primary" href="/quantum-information-degree-requirements" target="_blank" title="learn more about Quantum Information">Learn More</a></p></div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="col-sm-6">
<div class="panel panel-default">
<div class="panel-heading">
<h3 class="card-title">Machine Learning</h3>
</div>
<div class="panel-body">
<p class="card-text">Machine learning is a rapidly developing field within computer science. It is the study of algorithms that learn from data and experience.</p>
<p><a class="btn btn-primary" href="/machine-learning-degree-requirements" target="_blank" title="learn more about Machine Learning">Learn More</a></p></div>
</div>
</div>

                  <figcaption>Is Maryland Smith for Me?</figcaption>
              </figure>
      <p>The undergraduate experience at the Smith School is like no other. Our students proudly call it “The Smith Experience.”&nbsp;</p><p>From personal career coaching to the rare suite of activities only Smith offers, you’ll be able to check all the boxes necessary to build your own brand and command your career. You’ll be prepared to take on the responsibilities and intellectual challenges that a keen business sense requires. You’ll develop as a leader, but also have the interpersonal skills to be an invaluable teammate.</p><p><a class="btn btn-primary" href="https://www.admissions.umd.edu/apply/requirements/freshman" target="_blank">Apply Now</a>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="https://drive.google.com/file/d/164ldbD0WYTdduYVz0b6KIAVIuVcn7yga/view?usp=drive_link" target="_blank" rel="noopener">View Fact Sheet</a></p>

                      <h2>Policy Terps are bold problem solvers and fearless changemakers.</h2>
          
          
                                                                                                                <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vjVynLvfbOo" class="button button--cta">
          Watch Video: What is Public Policy?
        </a>
                        
  <!-- Render without, so quickedit/etc works -->
  

  
  <section>
      <h4>Be a dreamer. A creator. A leader. A changemaker.&nbsp;</h4><p>With no shortage of complex challenges, the world needs leaders&nbsp;who are able to understand and communicate the issues,&nbsp;who can&nbsp;design and implement bold solutions and&nbsp;who can&nbsp;ethically and compassionately lead the movements and organizations that create real change. As a Policy Terp, you will:</p><ul><li>Learn how to analyze the issues to create&nbsp;and critically evaluate responses that promote better outcomes for communities.&nbsp;</li><li>Cross disciplinary boundaries to better understand the complexities of the challenges the world faces and immerse yourself in multiple perspectives.</li><li>Develop decision-making and leadership skills to translate theory and analysis into on-the-ground action.</li></ul>
  </section>

          Get Started
        </a>

        </a>

  <hr class="spacer spacer--small">

<!-- Render without, so quickedit/etc works -->

  
  <section>
      <h3>A Career of Possibilities</h3><p>Public policy impacts every aspect of our society. At its core, every public issue has&nbsp;questions about our governing bodies and their relationships to people, organizations&nbsp;and the world around us. Studying public policy puts you at the heart of the issues, equipping you with the skills and knowledge to make a difference. Policy graduates are prepared to work across issues and sectors. Our graduates develop&nbsp;the most sought-after skills in the policy field today:&nbsp;strong analytical and decision-making&nbsp;skills, a creative approach to solving problems&nbsp;and&nbsp;a leadership style that is grounded in ethics and an appreciation for the multi-faceted nature of public issues.&nbsp;Policy Terps secure positions in all levels of government, in the private sector, in nonprofit and foundation organizations&nbsp;and&nbsp;in public service entities such as Peace Corps and AmeriCorps.&nbsp;</p>
  </section>

          Find out where public policy can take you
